It is said
that those of Shirkuh were only two thousand,
while the Franks and Egyptians were ten thousand.
Then Shirkuh went against Alexandria,
and took it without a battle.
The Egyptians and the Franks gathered in the city of Cairo,
and they sent to Shirkuh and sought peace.
And an agreement was concluded on the condition:
that fifty thousand dinars should be given to Shirkuh that he might go to his country,
and Alexandria would return again to the Egyptians;
and that one hundred thousand dinars should be given to the Franks each year,
and they would return to their country,
provided that they would have an overseer (shiḥna) and cavalry guards at the gates in Alexandria,
so that the house of Nur al-Din would be restrained from it.
And thus Shirkuh departed and went to Damascus.
And in this year, Qara Arslan, the lord of the fortress of Zaid (Hisn Ziyad), went against Amid,
and through the treachery of the guards, he gained control over two towers (bastions).
Those inside, however, took courage and killed those who had mounted the towers.
And Qara Arslan was put to shame,
and he returned to his country in sorrow and disgrace.
And after a little while he died on the 17th of Tammuz,
and his son arose after him.
And in the year
(1479 of the Greeks,
1168 of our Lord) {OCR?}, Toros, the ruler of Cilicia, died in the month of Kanon,
being a monk at the time of his death.
And he commanded
that his son, a small child, should succeed in his place,
and Thomas, his maternal aunt's son, should be his regent;
and his brother Mleh was completely excluded from the inheritance.
Then the latter was offended, and he went out to Nur al-Din {OCR?},
and took from him an army of Turks and entered Cilicia.
And he took captive sixteen thousand boys, girls, men, women, priests, monks, and bishops,
and carried them off to Aleppo.
And he sold them to the merchants,
and he gave their price to the Turks who were with him.
Then the Armenians sent and invited him to them,
and they gave him half of the country.
And he swore to them
that the other half should remain for the child.
Then he despised the oaths,
and gained control over all the country, fortresses, and cities.
And of many bishops and leaders he put out the eyes,
and cut off hands and feet,
and flayed others alive,
and cast them to wild beasts.
